extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 awards, their mentors, and institutional administrators
extracted.subtask_description: NIH peer-review criteria and reviewer guidance for K99/R00 Pathway to Independence applications, including the standard scored review categories and related administrative/evaluation considerations described in an NIH summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, training, record of productivity, and potential to develop into an independent investigator (e.g., 'Well trained candidate, currently on a T32 training grant'; reviewer scores such as 'Candidate: 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of research productivity (publications, awards), appropriate background for proposed research, demonstrated commitment to the research focus, and trajectory toward independence. Strengths and weaknesses should be noted (e.g., 'Well trained candidate...'; 'No weaknesses noted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals & Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the clarity, appropriateness, and strength of the proposed career development/training plan and the plan for mentoring (documented as 'Career Development Plan/Career Goals & Objectives' with reviewer scores such as '1' or '3').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether goals are complementary to the research aims, whether experiential and didactic training elements are present (clinical shadowing, grant-writing training, etc.), and whether mentoring/benchmarks are clearly specified. Watch for weaknesses like vague distinction between existing skills and gaps or lack of specific mentors (e.g., 'A geriatrician or clinician who does more work in health disparities ... would be helpful'; 'Mentorship letter read more like a wonderful support letter, as oppose to a necessary detailed letter with specific measures, benchmarks, etc.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the scientific plan including significance, specific aims, study design, methods (including measures and analyses), feasibility, power calculations, and handling of missing data (reported with reviewer scores such as 'Research Plan: 2' or '3').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect clear articulation of aims, detailed methods, justification of measures and analyses, power analyses with stated assumptions, consideration of sex as a biological variable, and plans for missing data/attrition. Note common weaknesses: brief/simplified conceptual framework, unclear rationale for power-analysis assumptions, insufficient analysis plan detail (e.g., handling heterogeneity, missing data), and unclear presentation of attrition allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the mentorship and advisory team’s expertise, track record, commitment, and appropriateness for the candidate's development (e.g., 'Mentors are established, well-known experts...'; reviewer scores like '1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether mentors provide complementary expertise, documented history of mentoring, plans for regular meetings, and inclusion of appropriate methodological/content experts. Look for problems such as letters that are supportive but lack specific mentoring plans, benchmarks, or measurable commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment, Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the institutional environment and resources available to the candidate and the institution’s commitment to support the candidate's transition to independence (reported as 'Environment, Commitment to the Candidate: 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability of research infrastructure, departmental support, clinical/community partnerships, and institutional plans for the R00 phase (e.g., consideration for a tenure-track position). Strength is noted when the environment is described as 'excellent' or 'superb.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers’ summary judgment of the project’s overall potential to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the field and to support the candidate's transition to independence (summarized as 'Overall Impact' with an Impact Score; e.g., 'This application is recommended with the highest enthusiasm.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact synthesizes criterion scores and discussion; reviewers note major strengths and weaknesses affecting likelihood of long-term success. The summary statement also contains the committee's final language about enthusiasm and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of human subjects protections, risk assessment, and adequacy of plans to minimize risks (e.g., 'Protections for Human Subjects: Acceptable. Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess consent/assent procedures, risk/benefit analysis, confidentiality, and procedures to protect vulnerable populations. Reviewer notes state whether protections are acceptable or raise concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the plan to monitor data and safety for the proposed human subjects research (noted as 'Data and Safety Monitoring Plan: Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an appropriate monitoring plan proportionate to study risk, accounting for institutional changes and trial design. Reviewers indicate acceptability or concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (Sex/Gender, Race/Ethnicity, Inclusion Across the Lifespan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of plans for inclusion of women, minorities, and children, and justification for participant distributions (sections labeled 'Inclusion Plans' with subitems: Sex/Gender; Race/Ethnicity; Inclusion/Exclusion of Children under 18; Inclusion Across the Lifespan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require scientific justification for distributions and sampling strategies (e.g., sampling equal numbers of African-American and Caucasian caregivers), and concrete estimates for expected demographic breakdowns. Reviewers mark plans as 'Acceptable' when justified; note special focus (e.g., disproportionate impact on African-American persons) and planned sampling strategies. Inclusion across lifespan should justify exclusion of minors when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the planned activities to satisfy RCR training requirements (noted as 'Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research: Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that planned RCR activities meet NIH requirements and are appropriate in format/duration/frequency. Reviewers note acceptability and may comment on appropriateness of format, subject matter, and faculty participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of plans for sharing data, tools, and resources resulting from the project (noted as 'Resource Sharing Plans: Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether resource sharing plans are adequate and consistent with institute/policy expectations; reviewers indicate acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the requested budget and recommended period of support (e.g., 'Budget and Period of Support: Recommend as Requested'; 'COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS: The budget was recommended as requested.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may recommend budgets as requested or suggest adjustments; administrative staff will calculate final costs based on committee recommendations. Note: Administrative Budget Note explaining budgets may be adjusted by grants management staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/Format and Participation Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist-like comments on format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, frequency, and other administrative aspects (e.g., 'Comments on Format: Acceptable'; 'Comments on Subject Matter: Acceptable'; 'Comments on Faculty Participation: Acceptable'; 'Comments on Duration: Acceptable'; 'Comments on Frequency: Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are short reviewer judgments about procedural/formatting elements and participation commitments; applicants should follow FOA instructions and ensure format/participation details are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to Prior Review / Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the resubmission addressed concerns raised in prior reviews (noted as 'Resubmission: The candidate has been very responsive to the prior reviews.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether prior criticisms were satisfactorily addressed via revisions, additional justifications, or added expertise; strong responsiveness is viewed positively and can affect scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Process and Criterion Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural explanation of how scores are generated and used (e.g., 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers... and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains that criterion scores are assigned pre-meeting, overall impact scores are calculated post-discussion by averaging reviewers' overall scores and scaling, and percentile rankings may also be provided. Applicants and mentors should understand this process when interpreting summary statements.
